title: Graded syzygy bound for two-variable polynomial rings
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S=k[x_0,x_1]$, graded by total degree (S_d is the k-span of monomials of total degree d and S_d=0 for d<0), with the projective-line conventions of [def-sc-p1-standard]. If $M=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M_n$ is a finitely generated graded $S$-module (so $S_iM_j\subseteq M_{i+j}$), then there are finite graded free $S$-modules $F_0,F_1,F_2$ and an exact sequence of graded modules $0\to F_2\to F_1\to F_0\to M\to0$. Each $F_i$ is a finite direct sum of graded shifts $S(d)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-free-cover] to M to construct F_0, its homogeneous basis and the graded surjection q_0.

Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-kernel-internal] to q_0. Scalar compatibility is inherited through the kernel inclusion. Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-free-cover] to ker(q_0), producing F_1 and q_1:F_1 to ker(q_0).

Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-kernel-internal] to q_1 and [lem-sc-p1-second-syzygy-tor-vanishes] to the two finite free covers. Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-free] to ker(q_1), using its inherited grading and finite homogeneous spanning set, to obtain a finite homogeneous basis.

Set F_2=ker(q_1), f_2 to its subtype inclusion, f_1 to the composite of q_1 with the inclusion of ker(q_0), and f_0=q_0. Prove range(f_1)=ker(f_0) by surjectivity of q_1, and range(f_2)=ker(f_1) by injectivity of the first-kernel inclusion. The second-kernel inclusion is injective. All maps preserve inherited degrees. Package the objects, gradings, ranks, shifts and bases by dependent case analysis on Fin 3; negate the third basis degrees for the shift convention.
